Make complicated things understandable.

Who it’s for
People who need support with dense or unfamiliar written information, including people with learning differences, cognitive disabilities, or executive-function challenges.
The goal
Connect an accessible explanation to the original text and a manageable, reviewable action list.

Planned capabilities, not a released application. Availability, platforms, and pricing have not been announced.

THE EVERYDAY CHALLENGE

PlainPath starts
with a real need.

A letter may contain a decision, a deadline, exceptions, and instructions spread across several pages. A shorter summary is useful only if it preserves the details the person needs to make a decision.

Connect an accessible explanation to the original text and a manageable, reviewable action list.

HOW IT COULD WORK

A thoughtful path
through the moment.

This walkthrough illustrates the intended experience. It describes the product direction, not functionality available on this website.

  1. Bring in the document

    Photograph or upload a letter, form, or set of instructions. The planned experience would flag unclear text rather than silently filling in missing information.

  2. Understand it in context

    Read an accessible explanation, look up an unfamiliar term, or listen aloud. Return to the source wording when a detail matters.

  3. Review the next steps

    Check extracted deadlines and actions. Prepare an editable response or choose a reminder after confirming the underlying requirement.

PLANNED CAPABILITIES

The details
we’re exploring.

  • Photograph or upload letters, forms, and instructions.
  • Explain complex language and unfamiliar terms in accessible wording.
  • Highlight required actions and stated deadlines.
  • Turn information into step-by-step checklists and reminders.
  • Offer read-aloud support, adjustable reading levels, and visual formatting.
  • Draft responses for the user to review and approve.

AN EVERYDAY EXAMPLE

What support could look like.

An insurance letter could become a plain-language explanation with its stated deadline and a checklist of possible next steps tied to the original document.

A design consideration

Explanations should preserve access to the original wording and distinguish stated facts from suggestions. Important deadlines and requirements would need verification.

ACCESSIBILITY & CONTROL

Designed around
the person using it.

Adjustable reading complexity, read-aloud support, spacing, and step-by-step views would let people choose how to approach the same information.

Privacy, affordability, and user autonomy are shared Biro.dev design principles. Product-specific data practices, supported access methods, and any offline capabilities would be explained before public release.

Read our design commitments

QUESTIONS ABOUT PLAINPATH

A clearer picture.

Would simplifying a document change its meaning?

The goal is to preserve meaning while making the language easier to understand. AI can make mistakes, so access to the original document and checks for important details are central to the concept.

Would PlainPath provide professional advice?

The concept focuses on explaining supplied information and organizing possible actions. It is not presented as a substitute for legal, medical, financial, or other professional advice.

Could it complete forms for me?

Drafting responses for review is planned. Automatic filing, signing, or submitting forms is not an announced capability.

When can I use PlainPath?

PlainPath is in early concept development. There is no public release date, price, or supported-platform list yet. The next step is to develop and evaluate the intended experience.
